title: The Great Persecution of Christians begins
summary: On the feast of the Terminalia, imperial troops destroyed the new church at Nicomedia, and the next day an edict ordered churches and scriptures destroyed across the empire.
reason: Diocletian and his Caesar Galerius saw the growing Christian church as a threat to the unity and traditional religion of the empire.
significance: It was the last and most severe persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire.
